source_text: Ἀνὴρ φοβερὸς εἶναι ὀφείλων τοῖς πολεμίοις, γέλωτός ἐστιν ἀφορμὴ τοῖς κατ' ἀγορὰν παιδίοις· ἄνευ σιδήρου καταβέβληται, ἄνευ πολεμίων πεφόνευται. Ἀνὴρ ὁπλίτης, αὐτὸ τῆς ἡλικίας ἄγων τὸ ἄνθος, οἴνου γέγονε παρανάλωμα, ἕτοιμος παθεῖν τοῖς ἐχθροῖς ὅσα βούλονται. Μέθη, λογισμῶν ὄλεθρος, ἰσχύος διαφθορὰ, γῆρας ἄωρον, ὀλιγοχρόνιος θάνατος. Τί γὰρ ἄλλο εἰσὶν οἱ μεθύοντες ἢ τὰ εἴδωλα τῶν ἐθνῶν; Ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχουσι, καὶ οὐ βλέπουσιν· ὦτα ἔχουσι, καὶ οὐκ ἀκούουσι· χεῖρες παραλέλυνται, οἱ πόδες ἀπενεκρώθησαν. Τίς ὁ ταῦτα ἐπιβουλεύσας; τίς ὁ τῶν κακῶν τούτων αἴτιος; τίς ὁ τὸ τῆς μανίας ἡμῖν φάρμακον ἐγκεράσας; Ἄνθρωπε, παρά ταξιν ἐποίησας τὸ συμπόσιον. Ἐκβάλλεις τοὺς νεανίσκους χειραγωγουμένους, ὡς τραυματίας ἀπὸ πολέμου· ἐνέκρωσας τὴν ἀκμὴν τῆς νεότητος ἀπὸ οἴνου· καὶ καλεῖς μὲν ὡς φίλον ἐπὶ τὸ δεῖπνον, ἐκβάλλεις δὲ νεκρὸν, οἴνῳ τὴν ζωὴν αὐτοῦ κατασβέσας. Ὅταν δὲ νομισθῶσι διακορεῖς εἶναι τοῦ οἴνου, τότε τοῦ πίνειν ἄρχονται, καὶ πίνουσι τὸν τῶν κτηνῶν τρόπον, ὡς ἀπὸ κρήνης αὐτοσχεδίου, ἰσαρίθμους τοῖς ἀνακειμένοις τοὺς κρουνοὺς ἀφιείσης. Προϊόντος γὰρ ἤδη τοῦ πότου, ἐπεισέρχεταί τις αὐτοῖς νεανίας, γενναῖος τοὺς ὤμους, οὔπω μεθύων, φιάλην φέρων εὐμεγέθη οἴνου κατεψυγμένου· ὃς, τὸν οἰνοχόον αὐτῶν παρωσάμενος, καταστὰς εἰς τὸ μέσον, διὰ σκολιῶν σωλήνων ἴσην τοῖς συμπόταις διανέμει τὴν μέ-θην. Καινὸν τοῦτο τῆς ἀμετρίας τὸ μέτρον, ἵνα κατ' ἰσομοιρίαν ἀλλήλοις συνασελγαίνωσι, μηδένα ὑπερβάλλειν ἐν τῷ πίνειν τὸν ἕτερον. Διελόμενοι γὰρ τὰς ὑδροῤῥόας, καὶ τὴν πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ἕκαστος τετραμμένην ὑποδεξάμενοι, ὥσπερ ἀπό τινος δεξαμενῆς ἀπνευστὶ πίνουσιν ὡς οἱ βόες, τοσοῦτον ὑφέλκειν ἐπειγόμενοι τοῖς λαιμοῖς, ὅσον αὐτοῖς ἄνωθεν ὁ ψυκτὴρ διὰ τῶν ἀργυρέων ὀχετῶν ἐπαφίησι. Κατά-κυψόν σου πρὸς τὴν ἀθλίαν γαστέρα· κατάμαθε τοῦ ὑποδεχομένου ἀγγείου τὸ μέγεθος· ὅτι μιᾶς κοτύλης ἔχει κοιλότητα. Μὴ πρὸς τὴν οἰνοχόην ἀφόρα, πότε κενώσῃς, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὴν σεαυτοῦ κοιλίαν, ὅτι πάλαι πεπλήρωται. Διὰ τοῦτο, Οὐαὶ οἱ ἐγειρόμενοι τὸ πρωῒ καὶ τὸ σίκερα διώκοντες, οἱ μένοντες τὸ ὀψὲ, καὶ διημερεύοντες ἐν τῇ μέθῃ· ὡς μηδένα καιρὸν ἑαυτοῖς παρέχειν εἰς τὸ τὰ ἔργα Κυρίου ἐμβλέπειν. καὶ τὰ ἔργα τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ κατανοεῖν. Ὁ γὰρ οἶνος αὐτοὺς συγκαύσει· διότι τὸ ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου θερμὸν, ἐγγινόμενον τῇ σαρκὶ, ἔξαμμα γίνεται τῶν πεπυρωμένων βελῶν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ. Τὸν μὲν γὰρ λογισμὸν καὶ τὸν νοῦν ὁ οἶνος καταβαπτίζει· τὰ δὲ πάθη καὶ τὰς ἡδονὰς ὥσπερ τι σμῆνος μελισσῶν ἐπεγείρει. Ποῖον γὰρ ἅρμα πώλων οὕτως ἀτάκτως φέρεται, ἀποβαλὸν τὸν ἡνίοχον; Ποῖον δὲ πλοῖον ἀκυβέρνητον, ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων, ὡς ἂν τύχῃ, φερόμενον, οὐκ ἀσφαλέστερόν ἐστι τοῦ μεθύοντος; Ἀπὸ τοιούτων κακῶν, ἄνδρες ὁμοῦ καὶ γυναῖκες, κοινοὺς συστησάμενοι χοροὺς, δαίμονι οἰνηρῷ τὰς ψυχὰς παραδόντες, ἀλλήλους ταῖς ἀκίσι τῶν παθῶν ἀντετίτρωσκον. Γέλωτες παρ' ἀμφοτέρων, ᾄσματα αἰσχρὰ, σχήματα πορνικὰ, ἐρεθίζοντα πρὸς ἀσέλ-γειαν. Γελᾷς, εἰπέ μοι, καὶ τέρπῃ τέρψιν ἀκόλαστον, δακρύειν δέον καὶ στένειν ἐπὶ τοῖς φθάσασιν; Ἄσματα πόρνης φθέγγῃ, ἐκβαλὼν τοὺς ψαλμοὺς καὶ τοὺς ὕμνους, οὓς ἐδιδάχθης. Κινεῖς πόδας, καὶ ἐξάλλῃ ἐμμανῶς, καὶ χορεύεις ἀχόρευτα, δέον τὰ γόνατα κάμπτειν εἰς τὴν προσκύνησιν; Τίνας ὀδύρωμαι; τὰς κόρας τὰς ἀπειρογάμους; ἢ τὰς ἐν τῷ ζυγῷ τοῦ γάμου κατεχομένας; Αἱ μὲν γὰρ ἐπανῆλθον, τὴν παρθενίαν οὐκ ἔχουσαι· αἱ δὲ τὴν σωφροσύνην τοῖς ἀνδράσιν οὐκ ἐπανήγαγον.
thought_title: Drunkenness as voluntary death and the mechanics of the drinking party
orientation: Basil continues his rebuke of drunkenness, now describing how a strong young soldier is undone by wine, how the drinking party is engineered so that all drink equally, and how this behavior destroys both men and women.
pass_a_gloss: A man who ought to be fearsome to enemies is an occasion of laughter to the children in the marketplace; without iron he has been struck down, without enemies he has been slain. A man-at-arms, bearing the very flower of his age, has become a casualty of wine, ready to suffer from his enemies whatever they wish. Drunkenness, destruction of reasonings, corruption of strength, untimely old age, short-lived death. For what else are the drunkards than the idols of the nations? They have eyes, and they do not see; they have ears, and they do not hear; their hands are paralyzed, their feet have been made dead. Who is the one who plotted these things? Who is the cause of these evils? Who is the one who mixed for us the drug of madness? Man, you made the drinking party out of order. You cast out the young men led by the hand, like wounded men from war; you killed the prime of youth with wine; and you invite him as a friend to dinner, but you cast him out a corpse, having quenched his life with wine. But when they are thought to be sated with wine, then they begin to drink, and they drink in the manner of beasts, as from an improvised spring, sending forth spouts equal in number to those reclining. For as the drinking advances, there comes in to them a young man, noble in shoulders, not yet drunk, carrying a large bowl of chilled wine; who, pushing aside their cupbearer, standing in the middle, through crooked pipes distributes equal drunkenness to the fellow drinkers. This is a new measure of excess, that by equal share they may commit outrage together, that no one may surpass the other in drinking. For dividing the water pipes, and each one receiving the one turned toward himself, they drink without drawing breath like oxen from some cistern, eager to draw down with their throats as much as the cooler sends forth to them from above through the silver channels. Bend down to your wretched stomach; learn the size of the vessel that receives; that it has the hollow of one cup. Do not look to the wine pourer, when you may empty it, but to your own belly, that it has long been filled. Therefore, Woe to those who rise early and pursue strong drink, those who stay late, and spend the whole day in drunkenness; so as to give themselves no time to look upon the works of the Lord and to consider the works of his hands. For the wine will burn them up; because the heat from the wine, coming into the flesh, becomes kindling for the fiery darts of the enemy. For the wine drowns the reasoning and the mind; but it rouses the passions and pleasures like a swarm of bees. For what chariot of colts is borne so disorderly, having thrown off its charioteer? And what ship without a pilot, borne by the waves as it may chance, is not safer than the drunkard? From such evils, men together with women, having formed common choruses, having handed over their souls to a winey demon, wounded one another with the barbs of the passions. Laughter from both, shameful songs, whorish postures, provoking to lust. You laugh, tell me, and delight in a licentious delight, when you ought to weep and groan over what has already happened? You utter the songs of a prostitute, having cast out the psalms and hymns which you were taught. You move your feet, and leap madly, and dance things not to be danced, when you ought to bend your knees in worship? Whom shall I lament? The unmarried maidens? Or those held in the yoke of marriage? For the former returned not having their virginity; the latter did not bring back their chastity to their husbands.

choices.why: keeps the military metaphor of a soldier consumed or expended by wine, matching the surrounding war imagery
literal rendering preserves the paradox of premature aging Basil uses to describe drunkenness
literal rendering keeps the oxymoron of a death that lasts only a short time, as Basil describes the state of the drunkard
echoes the Septuagint language of Psalm 113/115, which Basil is quoting, and keeps the biblical resonance
preserves the compound force of συν- (together) with ἀσελγαίνω (act outrageously), which Basil coins or uses to describe mutual shamelessness
rejected: they may act lewdly with one another

choices.why: literal rendering of the unusual adjective οἰνηρός keeps Basil's vivid personification of drunkenness as a demon made of wine

pass_b_english: A man who ought to be a terror to his enemies becomes a laughingstock for the children in the marketplace. He has been struck down without iron; he has been killed without enemies. A soldier in the very flower of his age has become a casualty of wine, ready to suffer whatever his enemies wish. Drunkenness is the ruin of reason, the corruption of strength, an untimely old age, a short-lived death. What else are drunkards but the idols of the nations? They have eyes, but they do not see; they have ears, but they do not hear (Psalm 115:5-7). Their hands are paralyzed; their feet have been made dead. Who plotted this? Who is responsible for these evils? Who mixed for us this drug of madness? You, sir, have made the drinking party contrary to all order. You send the young men out led by the hand, like wounded men from war. You have killed the prime of their youth with wine. You invite them to dinner as a friend, and you send them out as corpses, having quenched their life with wine. When they are thought to be sated with wine, that is when they begin to drink. They drink the way cattle do, as if from a makeshift spring that sends out as many spouts as there are guests reclining. As the drinking goes on, a young man comes in among them, broad-shouldered, not yet drunk, carrying a large bowl of chilled wine. He pushes their wine-pourer aside, stands in the middle, and through crooked pipes distributes equal drunkenness to the drinking companions. This is a new measure of excess: that they may commit outrage together in equal shares, so that no one outdrinks another. They divide the channels, and each one takes the one turned toward himself, and they drink without drawing breath like oxen from a cistern, each straining to pull down with his throat as much as the cooler above releases through the silver conduits. Look down at your wretched stomach. Take note of the size of the vessel that receives it: it has the hollow of a single cup. Do not stare at the wine jug, waiting to empty it; look at your own stomach, because it was filled long ago. Therefore: Woe to those who rise early in the morning and chase after strong drink, who linger late into the evening and spend the whole day in drunkenness (Isaiah 5:11), so that they give themselves no time to look at the works of the Lord or consider the works of His hands (Isaiah 5:12). For the wine will burn them, because the heat from the wine, entering the flesh, becomes kindling for the enemy's flaming arrows. Wine drowns reason and the mind, but it stirs up the passions and pleasures like a swarm of bees. What chariot of colts, having thrown off its driver, is carried along so wildly? What pilotless ship, borne by the waves wherever chance takes it, is not safer than a drunkard? From such evils, men and women together formed common choruses, handed their souls over to a winey demon, and wounded one another with the barbs of the passions. Laughter from both sides, shameful songs, prostitute's postures, inciting to lust. Tell me, do you laugh and take pleasure in unrestrained pleasure, when you ought to weep and groan over what has already happened? You sing a prostitute's songs, having thrown out the psalms and hymns you were taught. You move your feet and leap about madly and dance dances that should not be danced, when you ought to bend your knees in worship. Whom should I lament? The unmarried girls, or the women held under the yoke of marriage? The former came home no longer possessing their virginity; the latter did not bring their chastity back to their husbands.

problems.quote: You, sir, have turned the drinking party into a battle line out of order
problems.source_quote: Ἄνθρωπε, παρά ταξιν ἐποίησας τὸ συμπόσιον
problems.why: 'παρά ταξιν' means 'contrary to order/against rank,' not 'battle line out of order.'
problems.fix: You, sir, have made the drinking party contrary to all order.

edits.old: You, sir, have turned the drinking party into a battle line out of order.
edits.new: You, sir, have made the drinking party contrary to all order.

fixed: Corrected 'παρά ταξιν' to 'contrary to all order' rather than 'battle line out of order'; the phrase means 'against order/rank,' not a military formation.

last_rejected.quote: have made the drinking party contrary to all order
last_rejected.why: παρὰ τάξιν means 'contrary to order/rank', not 'contrary to all order'; 'all' is added.
last_rejected.fix: have made the drinking party contrary to order
last_rejected.ruling: παρὰ τάξιν = 'contrary to order'; 'all' is interpretive padding, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: They have eyes, but they do not see; they have ears, but they do not hear (Psalm 115:5-7)
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχουσι, καὶ οὐ βλέπουσιν· ὦτα ἔχουσι, καὶ οὐκ ἀκούουσιν
last_rejected.why: Basil quotes idols of nations, not Psalm 115 directly; attribution misleading.
last_rejected.fix: They have eyes, but they do not see; they have ears, but they do not hear.
last_rejected.ruling: Ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχουσι matches Psalm 115 LXX; parenthetical reference is standard, not misleading.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὰ εἴδωλα τῶν ἐθνῶν; Ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχουσι, καὶ οὐ βλέπουσιν· ὦτα ἔχουσι, καὶ οὐκ ἀκούουσιν
last_rejected.why: Basil alludes to idol language, not directly citing Psalm 115; wrong reference.
last_rejected.fix: Remove the Psalm reference or note it as an allusion to idol descriptions.
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ εἴδωλα τῶν ἐθνῶν introduces Psalm 115:5-7 language; reference is appropriate, not wrong.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'remain until evening,' not 'linger late into the evening.'
last_rejected.ruling: οἱ μένοντες τὸ ὀψέ means staying/lingering late; 'linger late into the evening' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: and spend the whole day in drunkenness
last_rejected.why: English loses 'spending the day' sense; 'whole day' is interpretation.
last_rejected.fix: and spend the day in drunkenness
last_rejected.ruling: διημερεύοντες means spending the whole day; 'spend the whole day' is accurate, not mere interpretation.

last_rejected.why: 'Drowns' overstates; καταβαπτίζει means submerges/overwhelms, not kills.
last_rejected.ruling: καταβαπτίζει literally means dip/submerge; 'drowns' is within normal range for metaphor of wine overwhelming reason.
